what: The copy-or-change table splits method names mid-token: 'a.reverse(' / ')', 'a.toRevers' / 'ed()', 'a.splice(s' / 'tart,' — a beginner reads them as two words.
evidence: crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c21-p11.png; cause assets/ext/js-ch21.css:66 `table.copy21 code { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` inside a 3-column table ~120px per column at 390.
fix: `table.copy21 code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` → `overflow-wrap: normal` plus wrap the table in `<div class="tablewrap">` and at ≤560px stack rows the way js-ch23.css `.tablewrap .mini` does (labels from the header) (code tokens must never break inside a name).

what: In the character-class table the hole `[A-C]` breaks into `[A-` / `C]` in the first column.
evidence: crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c22-p19.png; js-ch22.css:51 drops `white-space: nowrap` from `td:first-child` at ≤520px and :49 sets `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on code.
fix: `@media (max-width:520px) { table.ref22 td:first-child { white-space: normal } }` → keep `white-space: nowrap` on the first column (its tokens are ≤8 characters) and let the description column wrap (short regex tokens must stay whole).

what: The 'which way to wait' cheat sheet squeezes the method column so `Promise.all` prints as 'Pro/mise/.al/l' and `Promise.allSettled` as five fragments, the opposite of a cheat sheet.
evidence: crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c24-p36.png; js-ch24.css:62 `.pick24 code { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` in a 3-column table (the Use column is ~30px wide at 390).
fix: `.pick24 code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` → `white-space: nowrap` on the Use column's code, and at ≤560px stack each row as a card (Use as the card heading) (a method name is one token; never break it).

what: The kitchen cheat sheet breaks `process.nex|tTick(fn)`, `queueMicrot|ask(fn)` and `setImmediat|e(fn)` mid-name in the first column.
fix: Same fix as ch24 P36: `.pick25 code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` → `overflow-wrap: normal` with `<wbr>` after the `.`, and stack the table into cards at ≤560px (keep API names whole).

what: The stencil drawing's flag switches label their state ON/OFF at 9.4–10.5px (8px on the cover), below the 12px floor; those words are the declared non-colour carrier of the flag state.
evidence: audit: P16 'OFF' 9.4px at 390, 10.5px at 1280; P36 'ON' 9.4px; cover 'ON' 8px, 'STENCIL' 9.1px. crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c22-p16.png. js-ch22.js stencil: font-size="14" in a 440-unit viewBox drawn ~250–330px wide.
fix: stencil switch text `font-size="14"` → `font-size="19"` (and STENCIL 16 → 20), or give `.figs22` stencil figures a full row (`grid-column: 1 / -1`) (state words must reach 12px at every width).

what: The 'HUH?!' sound-effect burst covers the end of the caption ('reversing') and part of the inline code `split("").reverse().join("")`.
evidence: crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c22-p11.png; audit overlap 'HUH?!' vs caption text, 45% of the smaller box.
fix: Give this caption `max-width: calc(100% - 120px)` at ≤640px, or move the burst to `.sfx.tl` over the panel number side (an SFX must never sit on words).

what: The slider frame animates `left` (a layout property) over 350ms with the built-in `ease`; it is on-screen movement on every Next press, so it should be transform-based, use the movement tokens and stay ≤280ms.
evidence: js-ch22.css:69 `.slide-frame { … transition: left 0.35s ease }`; computed transition at 1280 with motion on: 'left 0.35s'. Reduced motion and 'Animations: off' correctly give 'none' (:74–75).
fix: `transition: left 0.35s ease` → position the frame with `transform: translateX(calc(var(--at) * 100%))` and `transition: transform var(--dur-move) var(--ease-in-out)` (GPU-only property, under the 300ms UI budget, strong curve for on-screen movement).

what: The timeline bars play their grow animation at page load, so it has finished long before anyone scrolls to Panel 10 (the explanatory motion is never seen); it also runs 600ms + up to 0.5s stagger with built-in ease-out from scaleX(0.05).
evidence: js-ch25.css:71 `.motion .tl25-bar { animation: tl25-grow 600ms ease-out both; animation-delay: var(--d) }` (js-ch25.js:177 sets --d = k*0.25s); the section has no data-play, so nothing gates it on visibility.
fix: `.motion .tl25-bar { animation: tl25-grow 600ms ease-out both }` → add `data-play` to the panel and use `.motion .panel.played .tl25-bar { animation: tl25-grow var(--dur-move) var(--ease-out) both; animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 60ms) }` with the keyframe from `scaleX(0.6); opacity: 0` (play when visible, under 300ms, 30–80ms stagger, no near-zero scale).

what: On phones each timeline is forced to min-width 480px inside a hand-rolled scroller with no 'Swipe sideways' hint, so the one-by-one timeline looks cut off after 'salad'; its ruler labels are 10.2–11px.
evidence: crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c25-p10.png; js-ch25.css:74 `.tl25-stage { overflow-x: auto } .tl25-stage svg { min-width: 480px }`; audit small text 'milliseconds' 10.2px, '0' 11px.
fix: `.tl25-stage { overflow-x: auto }` → wrap the svg as the engine's `<div class="picscroll"><svg class="pic-wide">` (560px, built-in swipe hint) and raise the ruler text to 14 units (use the engine pattern; labels ≥12px).

what: The triage desk drawing shrinks to 358px, so its sign texts render at 7.9px ('catch it here'), 9.5px ('EXIT') and 11.6px ('DISCHARGE: finally, tidy up').
evidence: crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c24-p2.png; audit small-text list for p2. The three cards below repeat the meaning, so it still reads.
fix: `.desk24 .char { max-width: 640px }` → wrap it as `<div class="picscroll">` with `class="pic-wide"` on the svg, or raise the sub-sign font-size attributes in js-ch24.js triagedesk from ~13 to 22 units (labels ≥12px on phones).

what: The three machines on the phone belt are squeezed into a 110px column, so their name plates ('trim', 'lower', 'dashes') render at 9px.
evidence: audit small text p23 'trim'/'lower'/'dashes' 9px; js-ch21.css:45 `.belt21 .stop { grid-template-columns: 110px minmax(0, 1fr) }`.
fix: `.belt21 .stop { grid-template-columns: 110px minmax(0,1fr) }` → `150px minmax(0,1fr)` (the machine at ≥150px keeps its plate ≥12px; the description column still has ~150px).

what: The chapter-local traystack and toybrick drawings label their contents below 12px: 'CALL STACK' 10.4px and tray calls 11px on the cover at both widths; the brick's '→ 35? 30? 25?' tag 9.9px and 'price(2)' 11.3px in P3 at 390.
evidence: crops /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c21-cover.png and /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c21-p3.png; js-ch21.js fit() minimum 11–12 units in a 340/230-unit viewBox drawn 170–220px wide.
fix: `.cover21 .char.tr { width: 220px }` → `width: 280px`, and in js-ch21.js raise fit()'s minimum from 11/12 to 16 units (labels on chapter characters ≥12px).

what: The small BigInt abacus at the end of Panel 21 shows its plate 'no Math' at 8.6px.
evidence: crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-21-25/c23-p21.png; audit 8.6px at both widths. bigabacus plate is 17 units in a 190-unit viewBox, drawn ~95px wide.

what: The spike name plate 'VIP' renders at 9.7px in Panel 2 (10.9px on the cover) and the cover pager tag '#25' at 9.6px.
evidence: audit small text: p2 'VIP' 9.7px, cover 'VIP' 10.9px, '#25' 9.6px; .kitchen25 .char 86px wide at ≤640px (js-ch25.css:35).
fix: `.kitchen25 figure .char { width: 86px }` → `width: 110px` at ≤640px (keeps the plate word ≥12px; the text column still fits).

what: Chapter tables and cards put `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on inline code, so API names split mid-token on phones (js ch21 P11, ch22 P19, ch24 P36, ch25 P35 in this batch); 100 files under assets/ext/ have a code rule with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. The engine has no stacked reference-table pattern, so each chapter improvises.
evidence: grep -l 'code[^{]*{[^}]*overflow-wrap: anywhere' assets/ext/*.css | wc -l → 100. js-ch23.css:94–100 (`.tablewrap .mini` stacked into cards at ≤560px) is the one version that reads well at 390.
fix: Per-chapter `table code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` → an engine `.ref-table` class: tokens `overflow-wrap: normal` with `<wbr>` after `.` and `(` (as the hanging-indent code already does), stacked into cards at ≤560px like js-ch23 `.mini` (one pattern; API names never break mid-word).

what: The catchphrase sticker `.catch` (yellow, rotated -1deg, hard shadow) and the `.duo-card.hot/.cool/.ok/.warn` tints are copied identically into 23 and 24 chapter stylesheets; the engine offers neither, though both are now house style.
evidence: grep -l '^\.catch {' assets/ext/*.css | wc -l → 23; grep -l '^\.duo-card\.warn' assets/ext/*.css | wc -l → 24 (js-ch21/22/24/25.css all carry both; js-ch23 has a renamed `.catch23`).
fix: 23 chapter copies of `.catch { … transform: rotate(-1deg) }` → one engine `.catch` using tokens (`--primary`, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-hard`) plus engine `.duo-card` tint modifiers; delete the chapter copies in the fix round (one component, one source).
